Heidelberg_Castle.past_comparison_summary: One of the most important Renaissance structures north of the Alps, now a poetic ruin.

Acropolis_of_Athens.name: Acropolis of Athens
Acropolis_of_Athens.description: Ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop
Acropolis_of_Athens.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Visitors: 16,000/day
-Major projects: Ongoing marble restoration
-Status: Symbol of Western Civilization
-Elevation: 150 m
Acropolis_of_Athens.statistics_text_past:
-Inhabited: Since 4th millennium BC
-Pericles' Era: Golden Age (5th C BC)
-Siege: Morosini's explosion in 1687
-Marbles: Lord Elgin's removal (1801)
-Significance: Sacred precinct to Athena
Acropolis_of_Athens.past_comparison_summary: The high city of Athens, evolving from a mycenaean fortress to the peak of classical Greek art.

Parthenon.name: Parthenon
Parthenon.description: Former temple on the Athenian Acropolis
Parthenon.statistics_text_present:
-Columns: 46 outer Doric columns
-Material: Pentelic marble
-Status: Most important surviving classical building
-Features: Optical illusions (entasis)
-Views: Visible from all over Athens
Parthenon.statistics_text_past:
-Completed: 438 BC
-Architects: Ictinus and Callicrates
-Sculptor: Phidias
-Conversions: Byzantine church, Catholic church, Mosque
-Damage: 1687 Venetian gunpowder explosion
Parthenon.past_comparison_summary: A temple of perfect proportions that has survived as a church, mosque, and enduring ruins.

Temple_of_Poseidon.name: Temple of Poseidon
Temple_of_Poseidon.description: Ancient Greek temple at Cape Sounion
Temple_of_Poseidon.statistics_text_present:
-Location: Atop a cliff 60 m above sea
-Remaining columns: 16
-Sunset: Famous for views over the Aegean
-Proximity: 70 km from Athens
-Material: Local marble
Temple_of_Poseidon.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 444–440 BC
-Era: Contemporary with Parthenon
-History: Graffito of Lord Byron (1810)
-Sacred: Dedicated to the God of the Sea
-Design: Hexastyle peripteral
Temple_of_Poseidon.past_comparison_summary: A dramatic coastal sanctuary marking the southernmost tip of the Attic peninsula.

Delphi.name: Delphi
Delphi.description: Sanctuary of Apollo and site of the Oracle
Delphi.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Key features: Temple of Apollo, Theater, Tholos
-Museum: Delphi Charioteer
-Setting: Slopes of Mount Parnassus
-Visitors: Major cultural destination
Delphi.statistics_text_past:
-Peak: 6th–4th century BC
-Role: Religious center of the Greek world
-The Oracle: Pythia giving prophecies
-Pythian Games: Precursor to Olympics
-Omphalos: Considered the center (navel) of the world
Delphi.past_comparison_summary: The most prestigious oracle in the ancient world, nestled in a stunning mountain landscape.

Meteora.name: Meteora
Meteora.description: Monastery complex built on natural sandstone rock pillars
Meteora.statistics_text_present:
-Active monasteries: 6 (out of original 24)
-UNESCO Site since: 1988
-Access: Steps carved into rock (modern)
-Tourism: World-famous hiking site
-Status: Second most important monastic group in Greece
Meteora.statistics_text_past:
-Origins: Hermit monks in 11th century
-Monastery building: 14th century (Byzantine era)
-Defense: Inaccessible except by nets and ladders
-Growth: Flourished during Ottoman occupation
-Significance: Safe haven for Orthodox tradition
Meteora.past_comparison_summary: Spiritual retreats 'suspended in the air', offering total isolation for centuries.

Palace_of_Knossos.name: Palace of Knossos
Palace_of_Knossos.description: Largest Bronze Age archaeological site on Crete
Palace_of_Knossos.statistics_text_present:
-Setting: Near Heraklion, Crete
-Highlights: Throne Room, Frescoes
-Visitors: 1 million/year
-Reconstruction: Controversial early 20th C work
-Status: Center of Minoan civilization
Palace_of_Knossos.statistics_text_past:
-Peak: 1700–1400 BC
-Mythology: Labyrinth and the Minotaur
-Architecture: Multi-story, plumbing, light wells
-Abandonment: Around 1350 BC
-Excavation: Sir Arthur Evans (1900)
Palace_of_Knossos.past_comparison_summary: The sophisticated labyrinthine palace of the Minoan kings, the first advanced civilization in Europe.

Great_Pyramid_of_Giza.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
Great_Pyramid_of_Giza.description: Oldest and largest of the pyramids in the Giza complex
Great_Pyramid_of_Giza.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 138.5 m (originally 146.6 m)
-Blocks: ~2.3 million stones
-UNESCO Site since: 1979
-Visitors: 14 million/year
-Status: Last of the Seven Wonders
Great_Pyramid_of_Giza.statistics_text_past:
-Built: ~2560 BC (Old Kingdom)
-Pharaoh: Khufu (Cheops)
-Facade: Originally covered in white limestone
-Peak: Capped with a gold pyramidion
-Construction: Built over ~20 years
Great_Pyramid_of_Giza.past_comparison_summary: The pinnacle of ancient engineering, once shining brilliant white under the desert sun.

Great_Sphinx_of_Giza.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
Great_Sphinx_of_Giza.description: Limestone statue of a reclining sphinx
Great_Sphinx_of_Giza.statistics_text_present:
-Length: 73 m
-Height: 20 m
-Face width: 4 m
-Restoration: Ongoing stabilization
-Orientation: Faces due east
Great_Sphinx_of_Giza.statistics_text_past:
-Built: ~2500 BC
-Subject: Likely Pharaoh Khafre
-Condition: Buried in sand for centuries
-Nose: Lost before the 18th century
-Features: Originally painted (traces of red/blue)
Great_Sphinx_of_Giza.past_comparison_summary: The world's oldest known monumental sculpture, guarding the pyramids for 4,500 years.

Karnak_Temple.name: Karnak Temple
Karnak_Temple.description: Vast open-air museum and religious site
Karnak_Temple.statistics_text_present:
-Area: 100 hectares
-Hypostyle Hall: 134 massive columns
-Location: Luxor (Ancient Thebes)
-Visitors: Top Egyptian cultural site
-Status: Second largest religious site ever
Karnak_Temple.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1971 BC – 30 BC
-Growth: Expanded by ~30 different Pharaohs
-God: Dedicated mainly to Amun-Ra
-Significance: Most important place of worship
-Lake: Sacred Lake for purification
Karnak_Temple.past_comparison_summary: A cumulative architectural history of Egypt's power, built over 1,500 years.

Abu_Simbel.name: Abu Simbel
Abu_Simbel.statistics_text_present:
-Relocation: Moved in 1968 (Aswan Dam project)
-Main Temple: 4 colossal statues of Ramses II
-UNESCO Site: Part of Nubian Monuments
-Sun Alignment: Oct 22 and Feb 22
-Location: Near the border with Sudan
Abu_Simbel.statistics_text_past:
-Built: ~1264 BC
-Commemorated: Ramses II's victory at Kadesh
-Construction: Carved directly into the cliff
-Discovery: Johann Ludwig Burckhardt (1813)
-Dedications: To Ra-Horakhty, Amun, and Ptah
Abu_Simbel.past_comparison_summary: The ultimate display of royal ego, successfully saved from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.

Valley_of_the_Kings.name: Valley of the Kings
Valley_of_the_Kings.description: Valley where tombs were excavated for pharaohs
Valley_of_the_Kings.statistics_text_present:
-Tombs: 63 discovered (KV1 to KV63)
-Most famous: Tutankhamun (KV62)
-Visitors: High limit per day
-UNESCO Site since: 1979
-Location: West Bank of the Nile
Valley_of_the_Kings.statistics_text_past:
-Era: New Kingdom (1550–1070 BC)
-Purpose: Hidden burials to avoid grave robbery
-Inhabitants: Ramses I-X, Seti I, Tutankhamun
-Decoration: Intricate wall paintings (Book of Dead)
-Labor: Deir el-Medina artisans village
Valley_of_the_Kings.past_comparison_summary: A hidden city of the dead, designed to protect the pharaohs' journey to the afterlife.

Luxor_Temple.name: Luxor Temple
Luxor_Temple.description: Large Ancient Egyptian temple complex on the East Bank
Luxor_Temple.statistics_text_present:
-Avenue: Avenue of Sphinxes (3 km to Karnak)
-Mosque: Abu Haggag (built on top)
-Night visit: Beautifully illuminated
-Obelisk: Only one left (companion in Paris)
-Status: Continuous place of worship
Luxor_Temple.statistics_text_past:
-Founded: ~1400 BC
-Key builders: Amenhotep III and Ramses II
-Function: Opet Festival center
-Significance: Coronation of Kings
-History: Served as a Roman fortress/camp
Luxor_Temple.past_comparison_summary: A temple that has stayed in use through Egyptian, Greek, Roman, Christian, and Islamic eras.

Great_Wall_of_China.name: Great Wall of China
Great_Wall_of_China.description: Ancient series of walls and fortifications
Great_Wall_of_China.statistics_text_present:
-Length: 21,196 km
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Visitors: 10 million/year (Badaling)
-Material: Stone, brick, tamped earth
-Status: New 7 Wonders of the World
Great_Wall_of_China.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 7th century BC – 17th century AD
-Main Dynasty: Ming (most preserved sections)
-Purpose: Protection against northern invasions
-Labor: Soldiers, peasants, prisoners
-Signal: Smoke and fire used for communication
Great_Wall_of_China.past_comparison_summary: A colossal defensive system that evolved over 2,000 years to become the symbol of Chinese endurance.

Forbidden_City.name: Forbidden City
Forbidden_City.description: Imperial palace complex in central Beijing
Forbidden_City.statistics_text_present:
-Area: 72 hectares
-Buildings: 980 surviving
-Visitors: 19 million/year (cap applied)
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Status: World's largest palace complex
Forbidden_City.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1406–1420 (Ming Dynasty)
-Function: Home of 24 Emperors
-Design: Traditional Chinese palatial architecture
-Color: Yellow (Imperial) and Red (Fortune)
-Access: Restricted to the imperial court for 500 years
Forbidden_City.past_comparison_summary: From a secluded center of divine imperial power to the world's most visited museum.

Terracotta_Army.name: Terracotta Army
Terracotta_Army.description: Collection of terracotta sculptures depicting the armies of Qin Shi Huang
Terracotta_Army.statistics_text_present:
-Figures: ~8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots
-Location: Xi'an
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Discovery: 1974 by local farmers
-Status: One of the greatest 20th C archaeological finds
Terracotta_Army.statistics_text_past:
-Created: ~210 BC
-Purpose: Protect the first Emperor in the afterlife
-Unique: Every face is different
-Original: Figures were brightly painted
-Weaponry: Real bronze swords and crossbows used
Terracotta_Army.past_comparison_summary: An underground silent army that remained hidden for two millennia to guard an emperor's tomb.

Summer_Palace.name: Summer Palace
Summer_Palace.description: Vast ensemble of lakes, gardens and palaces in Beijing
Summer_Palace.statistics_text_present:
-Area: 2.9 km² (3/4 is water)
-Main feature: Kunming Lake & Longevity Hill
-UNESCO Site since: 1998
-Style: Masterpiece of Chinese garden design
-Status: Former imperial garden
Summer_Palace.statistics_text_past:
-Origins: 1750 (Qing Dynasty)
-Destruction: 1860 by Anglo-French forces
-Reconstruction: Empress Dowager Cixi (1888)
-Symbolism: Harmony between man and nature
-Feature: The Long Corridor (728 m long)
Summer_Palace.past_comparison_summary: The ultimate imperial retreat, reflecting the aesthetic heights of the Qing dynasty's garden arts.

Temple_of_Heaven.name: Temple of Heaven
Temple_of_Heaven.description: Imperial complex of religious buildings in Beijing
Temple_of_Heaven.statistics_text_present:
-Main building: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests
-UNESCO Site since: 1998
-Park size: 2.7 km²
-Geometry: Circular buildings on square bases
-Status: Icon of Beijing architecture
Temple_of_Heaven.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1406–1420
-Purpose: Annual ceremonies for good harvest
-Symbolism: Circle (Heaven) and Square (Earth)
-Echo Wall: Famous acoustic properties
-Imperial: Visited by Emperors of Ming & Qing
Temple_of_Heaven.past_comparison_summary: A cosmic bridge between Earth and Heaven, where emperors once prayed for the prosperity of the empire.

Potala_Palace.name: Potala Palace
Potala_Palace.description: Winter palace of the Dalai Lamas since the 7th century
Potala_Palace.statistics_text_present:
-Elevation: 3,700 m (Lhasa, Tibet)
-Floors: 13
-Rooms: Over 1,000
-UNESCO Site since: 1994
-Status: Landmark of Tibetan Buddhism
Potala_Palace.statistics_text_past:
-Original: Built by Songtsen Gampo in 637 AD
-Current: Modern structure started 1645 (5th Dalai Lama)
-Parts: White Palace (secular) & Red Palace (religious)
-Defense: Massive stone walls up to 5 m thick
-Treasures: Golden stupas of past Dalai Lamas
Potala_Palace.past_comparison_summary: The spiritual and political heart of Tibet, towering over Lhasa from the Red Mountain.

Mount_Fuji.name: Mount Fuji
Mount_Fuji.description: Active stratovolcano and Japan's highest peak
Mount_Fuji.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 3,776 m
-UNESCO Site since: 2013
-Climbers: ~300,000/year
-Classification: Active (low risk)
-Status: Sacred symbol of Japan
Mount_Fuji.statistics_text_past:
-Formation: ~100,000 years ago
-Last eruption: 1707 (Hoei eruption)
-Religious: Goal of pilgrimages for centuries
-Art: Subject of Hokusai's '36 Views of Mt. Fuji'
-Traditional: First ascent by an anonymous monk (663 AD)
Mount_Fuji.past_comparison_summary: A timeless volcanic peak that has inspired Japanese art and spirituality for generations.

Fushimi_Inari-taisha.name: Fushimi Inari-taisha
Fushimi_Inari-taisha.description: Head shrine of the god Inari, famous for thousands of torii gates
Fushimi_Inari-taisha.statistics_text_present:
-Gates: Over 10,000 Torii
-Location: Kyoto
-Visitors: One of Japan's most photographed sites
-Messenger: Fox (Kitsune) statues
-Access: Always open, free entry
Fushimi_Inari-taisha.statistics_text_past:
-Founded: 711 AD
-Deity: Inari (God of rice and business)
-Torii: Custom of donating gates started in Edo period
-Patronage: Supported by merchants and manufacturers
-Structure: Main shrine built in 1499
Fushimi_Inari-taisha.past_comparison_summary: A mountain path of vermillion gates, built through centuries of devotion by those seeking prosperity.

Himeji_Castle.name: Himeji Castle
Himeji_Castle.description: Hilltop Japanese castle complex in Himeji
Himeji_Castle.statistics_text_present:
-Nickname: White Heron Castle
-UNESCO Site since: 1993
-Buildings: 83 original structures
-Status: Best preserved example of Japanese castle architecture
-Authenticity: Never destroyed by war or fire
Himeji_Castle.statistics_text_past:
-Built: Started 1333, expanded by Hideyoshi (1581)
-Defenses: Maze-like paths, 21 gates, hidden walls
-Material: Wood and white plaster
-WWII: Survived bombing of Himeji (miraculously)
-Symbolism: Elegant bird taking flight
Himeji_Castle.past_comparison_summary: A pristine wooden fortress that has survived nearly 700 years of history untouched.

Kinkaku-ji.name: Kinkaku-ji
Kinkaku-ji.description: Zen Buddhist temple with two floors covered in gold leaf
Kinkaku-ji.statistics_text_present:
-Nickname: Golden Pavilion
-Location: Kyoto
-UNESCO Site since: 1994
-Surrounding: Mirror Pond (Kyoko-chi)
-Status: Icon of Kyoto
Kinkaku-ji.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1397 (as villa for Ashikaga Yoshimitsu)
-Architecture: Three distinct styles per floor
-Tragedy: Burned down in 1950 by a fanatic monk
-Restoration: Rebuilt in 1955 (gold leaf added)
-Zen: Converted to temple after Shogun's death
Kinkaku-ji.past_comparison_summary: A stunning golden reflection of the Muromachi period's cultural extravagance and Zen simplicity.

Itsukushima_Shrine.name: Itsukushima Shrine
Itsukushima_Shrine.description: Shinto shrine known for its 'floating' torii gate
Itsukushima_Shrine.statistics_text_present:
-Location: Miyajima Island
-UNESCO Site since: 1996
-Gate height: 16 m
-High tide: Appears to float on water
-Status: One of the 'Three Views of Japan'
Itsukushima_Shrine.statistics_text_past:
-Founded: 593 AD
-Current buildings: From 1168 (Taira no Kiyomori)
-Sacred: Commoners weren't allowed on the island
-Construction: Built on piers to protect sacred land
-Gate: Current torii dates from 1875
Itsukushima_Shrine.past_comparison_summary: A spiritual masterpiece where the architecture harmonizes perfectly with the ebb and flow of the tide.

Tokyo_Tower.name: Tokyo Tower
Tokyo_Tower.description: Communications and observation tower in the Minato district
Tokyo_Tower.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 332.9 m
-Color: White and International Orange (aviation safety)
-Visitors: 150 million since opening
-Status: Symbol of Japan's post-war rebirth
-Inspiration: Eiffel Tower
Tokyo_Tower.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1958
-Function: TV and radio broadcasting
-Materials: 1/3 is scrap metal from US tanks
-History: Tallest structure in Japan until 2010
-Significance: Embodied the 'Economic Miracle'
Tokyo_Tower.past_comparison_summary: Japan's mid-century response to the Eiffel Tower, symbolizing a nation's rapid modernization.

Taj_Mahal.name: Taj Mahal
Taj_Mahal.description: Ivory-white marble mausoleum on the Yamuna river
Taj_Mahal.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 73 m
-Visitors: 7–8 million/year
-UNESCO Site since: 1983
-Status: New 7 Wonders of the World
-Location: Agra
Taj_Mahal.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1632–1653
-Commissioned: Emperor Shah Jahan
-Purpose: Tomb for wife Mumtaz Mahal
-Architect: Ustad Ahmad Lahauri
-Artisan: ~20,000 workers
Taj_Mahal.past_comparison_summary: The world's most famous monument to love, unchanged in its symmetrical marble perfection.

Hawa_Mahal.name: Hawa Mahal
Hawa_Mahal.description: Palace of the Winds in Jaipur
Hawa_Mahal.statistics_text_present:
-Windows: 953 small casements (Jharokhas)
-Material: Pink and red sandstone
-Height: 15 m (5 stories)
-Status: Landmark of the 'Pink City'
-Shape: Crown of Lord Krishna
Hawa_Mahal.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1799
-Architect: Lal Chand Ustad
-Purpose: For royal ladies to observe the street unseen
-Cooling: Venturi effect through small windows
-Structure: Extension of the City Palace
Hawa_Mahal.past_comparison_summary: An intricate pink facade designed to let the breeze and the world pass by royal seclusion.

Qutub_Minar.name: Qutub Minar
Qutub_Minar.description: 73-meter high tapering tower of five storeys
Qutub_Minar.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 72.5 m
-UNESCO Site since: 1993
-Material: Red sandstone and marble
-Steps: 379 inside (closed to public)
-Status: Tallest brick minaret in the world
Qutub_Minar.statistics_text_past:
-Started: 1192 (Qutb-ud-din Aibak)
-Completed: Over centuries by different rulers
-Complex: Contains Iron Pillar of Delhi (4th C)
-Style: Indo-Islamic architecture
-Inscriptions: Quranic verses carved in stone
Qutub_Minar.past_comparison_summary: A victory tower that witnessed the rise of Islamic rule in India over several centuries.

Golden_Temple.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
Golden_Temple.description: The preeminent spiritual site of Sikhism
Golden_Temple.statistics_text_present:
-Location: Amritsar
-Visitors: 100,000/day
-Langar: World's largest free kitchen
-Material: Covered in 750 kg of pure gold
-Status: Symbol of equality and brotherhood
Golden_Temple.statistics_text_past:
-Founded: 1577 (Guru Ram Das)
-Design: 4 entrances (open to all castes/creeds)
-Gold: Added by Maharaja Ranjit Singh (1830)
-Sarovar: The sacred pool surrounding the temple
-Reconstruction: Rebuilt several times after invasions
Golden_Temple.past_comparison_summary: A sanctuary of gold and peace, serving free meals to all as a testament to human equality.

Amer_Fort.name: Amer Fort
Amer_Fort.description: Large fort complex located on a hill in Amer, Rajasthan
Amer_Fort.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 2013 (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)
-Highlight: Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace)
-Access: Famous for elephant and jeep rides
-Location: 11 km from Jaipur
-Material: Yellow and pink sandstone
Amer_Fort.statistics_text_past:
-Built: Started 1592 (Raja Man Singh I)
-Style: Rajput and Mughal influences
-Defenses: Maota Lake providing natural barrier
-Interior: Opulent courtyards and frescoes
-History: Capital of the Kachwaha clan
Amer_Fort.past_comparison_summary: A majestic hilltop fortress blending rugged military defense with delicate artistic interior.

Ajanta_Caves.name: Ajanta Caves
Ajanta_Caves.statistics_text_present:
-Number of caves: 30
-UNESCO Site since: 1983
-Location: Maharashtra
-Highlight: Ancient frescoes and murals
-Status: Masterpieces of Buddhist religious art
Ajanta_Caves.statistics_text_past:
-Period: 2nd century BC – 480 AD
-Forgotten: Abandoned and hidden by jungle for 1,300 years
-Discovery: 1819 by a British officer
-Art: Jataka tales depicted in paintings
-Method: Carved into the basalt cliff side
Ajanta_Caves.past_comparison_summary: An ancient gallery of Buddhist faith, rediscovered by chance after being lost to the forest.

Christ_the_Redeemer.name: Christ the Redeemer
Christ_the_Redeemer.description: Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ in Rio de Janeiro
Christ_the_Redeemer.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 30 m (38 m with pedestal)
-Arms span: 28 m
-Location: Corcovado Mountain (710 m)
-Status: New 7 Wonders of the World
-Symbol: Icon of Rio and Brazil
Christ_the_Redeemer.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1922–1931
-Sculptor: Paul Landowski
-Material: Reinforced concrete and soapstone tiles
-Inauguration: Oct 12, 1931
-Lightning: Frequently struck due to mountain peak
Christ_the_Redeemer.past_comparison_summary: A colossal Art Deco guardian watching over Rio de Janeiro from the heavens.

Sugarloaf_Mountain.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
Sugarloaf_Mountain.description: Peak situated in Rio de Janeiro at the mouth of Guanabara Bay
Sugarloaf_Mountain.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 396 m
-Access: Glass-walled cable car (Bondinho)
-Visitors: 1.5 million/year
-UNESCO Site since: 2012 (Landscape category)
-View: 360-degree panorama of the city
Sugarloaf_Mountain.statistics_text_past:
-Formation: Granite and quartz monolith
-Cable Car: First built in 1912 (one of the world's oldest)
-Naming: Shape resembles traditional sugar molds
-Strategic: Landmark for sailors entering the bay
-History: Witnessed the founding of Rio in 1565
Sugarloaf_Mountain.past_comparison_summary: A unique geological monolith that has offered the world's best urban view for over a century.

Iguacu_Falls.name: Iguaçu Falls
Iguacu_Falls.description: Massive waterfalls of the Iguaçu River on the border with Argentina
Iguacu_Falls.statistics_text_present:
-Number of drops: 275
-UNESCO Site since: 1986
-Greatest drop: Devil's Throat (82 m)
-Width: 2.7 km
-Visitors: 2 million/year
Iguacu_Falls.statistics_text_past:
-Discovery: Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca (1541)
-Park: National Park created in 1939
-Nature: Surrounding Atlantic Forest sanctuary
-Mythology: Created by a god's rage (Naipí legend)
-Comparison: Taller than Niagara, wider than Victoria
Iguacu_Falls.past_comparison_summary: Nature's overwhelming power displayed through the world's largest waterfall system.

Amazon_Theatre.name: Amazon Theatre (Teatro Amazonas)
Amazon_Theatre.description: Opera house in Manaus, in the heart of the Amazon rainforest
Amazon_Theatre.statistics_text_present:
-Location: Manaus
-Capacity: 701 seats
-Style: Renaissance Revival
-Dome: Covered in 36,000 ceramic tiles (Brazilian colors)
-Status: Jewel of the Amazon
Amazon_Theatre.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1884–1896
-Era: The Rubber Boom (Belle Époque)
-Materials: Imported from all over Europe
-Inauguration: Jan 7, 1897
-Significance: Culture in the middle of the jungle
Amazon_Theatre.past_comparison_summary: A testament to the wealth of the rubber era, bringing European luxury to the rainforest.

Cathedral_of_Brasilia.name: Cathedral of Brasília
Cathedral_of_Brasilia.description: Hyperboloid structure serving as the seat of the Archdiocese of Brasília
Cathedral_of_Brasilia.statistics_text_present:
-Architect: Oscar Niemeyer
-Columns: 16 concrete columns (90 tons each)
-Style: Modernist
-Visitors: 1 million/year
-Status: Masterpiece of modern architecture
Cathedral_of_Brasilia.statistics_text_past:
-Completed: 1970
-Design: Reaching up to the heavens
-Interior: 3 hanging angel sculptures
-Light: Stained glass roof in blue and green
-Significance: Part of the planned capital project
Cathedral_of_Brasilia.past_comparison_summary: A revolutionary circular design that redefined religious architecture in Brazil's new capital.

Pelourinho.name: Pelourinho (Historic Centre of Salvador)
Pelourinho.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1985
-Architecture: Portuguese colonial buildings
-Colors: Pastel-colored facades
-Culture: Heart of Afro-Brazilian heritage
-Activities: Olodum drummers, Capoeira
Pelourinho.statistics_text_past:
-Origins: 1549 (Brazil's first capital)
-Name: Means 'Pillory' (site of slave punishment)
-Golden Age: 17th–18th century sugar trade wealth
-Church: São Francisco (famous for gold interior)
-Revitalization: Major restoration in the 1990s
Pelourinho.past_comparison_summary: The vibrant, colorful cradle of Brazilian culture, reflecting a complex colonial history.

Sydney_Opera_House.name: Sydney Opera House
Sydney_Opera_House.description: Multi-venue performing arts centre in Sydney Harbour
Sydney_Opera_House.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 2007
-Visitors: 10 million/year
-Tiles: 1,056,006 Swedish ceramic tiles
-Performance: ~1,500 events per year
-Status: 20th century architectural icon
Sydney_Opera_House.statistics_text_past:

-Controversy: Huge budget overruns and architect resignation
-Design: Shells inspired by orange segments
-Inauguration: Queen Elizabeth II (1973)
Sydney_Opera_House.past_comparison_summary: The sail-shaped masterpiece that transformed Sydney's waterfront into a world icon.

Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.description: Steel through arch bridge across Sydney Harbour

-Built: 1923–1932

-Rivets: 6 million (hand-driven)
-Depression era: Major source of employment
-Opening: Cut ribbon ceremony (March 1932)
Sydney_Harbour_Bridge.past_comparison_summary: An engineering feat of the 1930s that remains the sturdy backbone of Sydney's transport.

Uluru.name: Uluru (Ayers Rock)
Uluru.description: Massive sandstone monolith in the Northern Territory
Uluru.statistics_text_present:
-Height: 348 m
-Circumference: 9.4 km
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Color change: Appears to glow red at sunset
-Status: Deeply sacred to Anangu people
Uluru.statistics_text_past:
-Age: 550 million years
-Traditional owners: Anangu (land returned in 1985)
-Climbing: Permanently closed in 2019 (respect for culture)
-Rock Art: Ancient paintings in caves around the base
-Geology: Arkose sandstone monolith
Uluru.past_comparison_summary: The spiritual heart of Australia, standing as a silent monolith for half a billion years.

Great_Barrier_Reef.name: Great Barrier Reef
Great_Barrier_Reef.description: The world's largest coral reef system
Great_Barrier_Reef.statistics_text_present:
-Length: 2,300 km
-Reefs: ~2,900 individual reefs
-UNESCO Site since: 1981
-Fauna: 1,500 fish species, 30 whale/dolphin species
-Visibility: Visible from outer space
Great_Barrier_Reef.statistics_text_past:
-Formation: ~20,000 years (modern reef)
-Indigenous: Significant to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders
-History: Cook's Endeavour grounded in 1770
-Conservation: Protected by Marine Park since 1975
-Threats: Bleaching events due to ocean warming
Great_Barrier_Reef.past_comparison_summary: A living underwater masterpiece that has flourished for millennia, now facing modern challenges.

Port_Arthur.name: Port Arthur
Port_Arthur.description: Former convict settlement and open-air museum in Tasmania
Port_Arthur.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 2010 (Convict Sites)
-Buildings: 30 ruins and restored homes
-Status: Australia's most significant convict site
-Setting: Tasman Peninsula
-Ghost Tours: Famous for evening walks
Port_Arthur.statistics_text_past:
-Operating: 1833–1877
-Purpose: Prison for repeat offenders
-System: Separate Prison (silent system)
-Economy: Ship building and timber
-Aftermath: Became a tourist destination in late 19th C
Port_Arthur.past_comparison_summary: A chilling but beautiful reminder of Australia's penal colony origins.

Twelve_Apostles.name: Twelve Apostles
Twelve_Apostles.description: Collection of limestone stacks off the shore of Port Campbell National Park
Twelve_Apostles.statistics_text_present:
-Location: Great Ocean Road, Victoria
-Remaining stacks: 8 (others collapsed)
-Height: Up to 50 m
-Tourism: Major helicopter tour site
-Status: Iconic natural wonder
Twelve_Apostles.statistics_text_past:
-Formation: Erosion by Southern Ocean (10-20m years)
-Original Name: Sow and Pigs
-Renamed: To Twelve Apostles in the 1920s (marketing)
-Collapses: Most recent major stack fell in 2005
-Geology: Miocene limestone
Twelve_Apostles.past_comparison_summary: A dynamic coastline where the ocean constantly creates and destroys these majestic stone pillars.

Chichen_Itza.name: Chichen Itza
Chichen_Itza.description: Large pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people
Chichen_Itza.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1988
-Visitors: 2.6 million/year
-Main Pyramid: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcan)
-Status: New 7 Wonders of the World
-Location: Yucatán State
Chichen_Itza.statistics_text_past:
-Peak: ~600 AD to 1200 AD
-Astronomy: Pyramid aligns with equinox shadows
-Sacrifices: Sacred Cenote (sinkhole)
-Ball Game: Largest ball court in Mesoamerica
-Architecture: Puuc and Toltec influences
Chichen_Itza.past_comparison_summary: A sophisticated center of Mayan science and religion, reclaimed from the jungle.

Teotihuacan.name: Teotihuacan
Teotihuacan.description: Ancient Mesoamerican city known for its pyramids
Teotihuacan.statistics_text_present:
-Main structures: Pyramid of the Sun & Pyramid of the Moon
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Location: 40 km from Mexico City
-Status: Most visited archaeological site in Mexico
-Avenue: Avenue of the Dead
Teotihuacan.statistics_text_past:
-Peak: 1 AD to 500 AD (Population ~125,000+)
-Mystery: Builders unknown (Aztecs named the site)
-Sun Pyramid: One of the largest in the world
-Abandonment: Around 7th–8th century AD
-Ritual: Center of a vast multi-ethnic empire
Teotihuacan.past_comparison_summary: The 'Place where Gods were created', an urban marvel that predates the Aztecs by centuries.

Tulum.name: Tulum
Tulum.description: Pre-Columbian Mayan walled city serving as a port
Tulum.statistics_text_present:
-Location: Coastal cliff overlooking the Caribbean
-Status: Popular beach-side archaeological site
-Highlight: El Castillo (The Castle)
-Flora: Famous for iguanas living in ruins
-Climate: Tropical
Tulum.statistics_text_past:
-Peak: 13th to 15th centuries
-Function: Major trading hub (turquoise and jade)
-Defense: Enclosed by a 7 m thick wall
-Survival: One of the last Mayan cities to fall (1518)
-Astronomy: Temple of the Frescoes used for tracking sun
Tulum.past_comparison_summary: A picturesque Mayan fortress that combined maritime trade with spiritual defense.

Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes.description: The most important cultural center in Mexico City
Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes.statistics_text_present:
-Style: Art Nouveau exterior, Art Deco interior
-Murals: Rivera, Siqueiros, Orozco
-Status: National Theater of Mexico
-Material: White marble from Carrara
-Problem: Sinking slowly into the soft subsoil
Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes.statistics_text_past:
-Started: 1904 (Porfirio Díaz era)
-Architect: Adamo Boari
-Halt: Mexican Revolution (delayed 20 years)
-Completion: 1934
-Feature: Crystal curtain made by Tiffany
Palacio_de_Bellas_Artes.past_comparison_summary: A stunning marble temple of art that survived the revolution to become Mexico's cultural soul.

Chapultepec_Castle.name: Chapultepec Castle
Chapultepec_Castle.description: Hilltop castle in the middle of Chapultepec Park
Chapultepec_Castle.statistics_text_present:
-Function: National Museum of History
-Location: Top of Chapultepec Hill (Sacred place)
-Visitors: High cultural importance
-Status: Only royal castle in North America
-Views: Overlooking Paseo de la Reforma
Chapultepec_Castle.statistics_text_past:
-Built: 1785 (Viceroyalty of New Spain)
-History: Military Academy (Battle of Chapultepec 1847)
-Imperial: Home of Emperor Maximilian I (1864)
-Presidential: Official residence until 1939
-Architecture: Neoclassical and Neo-romantic
Chapultepec_Castle.past_comparison_summary: From a viceregal palace to an imperial residence and now a guardian of Mexico's history.

Palenque.name: Palenque
Palenque.description: Maya city state in southern Mexico that flourished in the 7th century
Palenque.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1987
-Location: Chiapas jungle
-Highlight: Temple of the Inscriptions
-Status: Famed for architectural elegance
-Excavation: Only ~10% of the city is visible
Palenque.statistics_text_past:
-Peak: 226 BC – 799 AD
-King: Pakal the Great (ruled 68 years)
-Discovery: Pakal's tomb found in 1952
-Art: Most sophisticated Mayan bas-reliefs
-Water: Sophisticated aqueduct system
Palenque.past_comparison_summary: A jungle-enshrouded masterpiece of Mayan architecture and historical records.

Machu_Picchu.name: Machu Picchu
Machu_Picchu.description: 15th-century Inca citadel located in the Eastern Cordillera
Machu_Picchu.statistics_text_present:
-Elevation: 2,430 m
-Visitors: ~1.5 million/year
-UNESCO Site since: 1983
-Status: New 7 Wonders of the World
-Access: Train to Aguas Calientes
Machu_Picchu.statistics_text_past:
-Built: ~1450 (Inca Empire)
-Purpose: Estate for Emperor Pachacuti
-Technique: Ashlar (dry stone walls)
-Abandonment: 1572 (post-Spanish conquest)
-Rediscovery: Hiram Bingham (1911)
Machu_Picchu.past_comparison_summary: The 'Lost City of the Incas', a stunning display of mountain engineering and astronomical alignment.

Sacsayhuaman.name: Sacsayhuaman
Sacsayhuaman.description: Citadel on the northern outskirts of the city of Cusco
Sacsayhuaman.statistics_text_present:
-Location: 3,700 m elevation
-Main attraction: Gigantic zigzag walls
-Stones: Largest weighs over 120 tons
-Status: Symbol of Inca military architecture
-Event: Inti Raymi festival (June 24)
Sacsayhuaman.statistics_text_past:
-Started: 15th century (Pachacuti expansion)
-Function: Fortress and ceremonial center
-Construction: Precise interlocking stones without mortar
-Siege: Site of bloody battle in 1536
-Destruction: Spanish used it as a stone quarry
Sacsayhuaman.past_comparison_summary: A colossal stone mystery where huge boulders fit together with surgical precision.

Nazca_Lines.name: Nazca Lines
Nazca_Lines.description: Group of very large geoglyphs formed in the soil of the Nazca Desert
Nazca_Lines.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1994
-Figures: Hummingbird, Monkey, Spider, Condor
-Length: Up to 370 m per figure
-Access: Best seen from small plane tours
-Area: 450 km²
Nazca_Lines.statistics_text_past:
-Created: 500 BC – 500 AD
-Method: Removing reddish pebbles to reveal gray soil
-Purpose: Religious or astronomical calendar (theories)
-Preservation: Hyper-arid climate (no wind/rain)
-Rediscovery: 1927 by Toribio Mejia Xesspe
Nazca_Lines.past_comparison_summary: Giant ancient drawings in the desert that can only be fully appreciated from the sky.

Plaza_de_Armas_Cusco.name: Plaza de Armas (Cusco)
Plaza_de_Armas_Cusco.description: The central square in the historic center of Cusco

-Highlight: Cusco Cathedral and Church of La Compañía
-Activity: Social heart of the city
-Architecture: Spanish colonial over Inca foundations
-Status: UNESCO World Heritage site (city-wide)
Plaza_de_Armas_Cusco.statistics_text_past:
-Inca era: Known as Huacaypata (Place of Mourning)
-Significance: Religious and administrative center of Empire
-Spanish era: Built churches over Inca palaces
-History: Execution site of Tupac Amaru II (1781)
-Evolution: From sacred Inca field to colonial plaza
Plaza_de_Armas_Cusco.past_comparison_summary: The epicenter of the Inca Empire, where colonial cathedrals now stand on the bones of sun temples.

Huaca_Pucllana.name: Huaca Pucllana
Huaca_Pucllana.description: Adobe and clay pyramid located in the Miraflores district of Lima
Huaca_Pucllana.statistics_text_present:
-Structure: Great Pyramid of 7 staggered levels
-Location: Modern urban center of Lima
-Material: Millions of 'book-shelf' style adobe bricks
-Status: Important ceremonial center
-Feature: High-end restaurant overlooking ruins
Huaca_Pucllana.statistics_text_past:
-Period: 200 AD – 700 AD (Lima Culture)
-Technique: Vertical brick placement (earthquake resistant)
-Function: Religious rituals and administration
-Succession: Later used by Wari and Ychsma cultures
-Burials: Mummies found in the upper levels
Huaca_Pucllana.past_comparison_summary: An ancient earthen pyramid standing in startling contrast to the modern skyscrapers of Lima.

Chan_Chan.name: Chan Chan
Chan_Chan.description: Largest adobe city in the world
Chan_Chan.statistics_text_present:
-UNESCO Site since: 1986 (List in Danger)
-Area: 20 km²
-Location: Near Trujillo
-Feature: Intricate relief carvings of fish and birds
-Climate: Arid coastal desert

-Capital: Chimú Kingdom
-Peak: ~850 AD to 1470 AD
-Population: ~30,000–60,000
-Conquest: Captured by Incas in 1470
-Water: Sophisticated system of wells and canals

CN_Tower.name: CN Tower

-Status: One of the modern Seven Wonders of the World

-Built: 1973–1976
-Commissioned: Canadian National Railway
-Purpose: Solving signal issues due to skyscrapers
-Record: Tallest free-standing structure for 32 years
-Engineering: Slipform construction method

Banff_National_Park.name: Banff National Park

Chateau_Frontenac.name: Château Frontenac

Peggy's_Cove.name: Peggy's Cove

Parliament_Hill.name: Parliament Hill

Niagara_Falls.name: Niagara Falls

-History: Strategic site in War of 1812
-Stunts: First barrel ride (Annie Edson Taylor, 1901)
-Erosion: Moving upstream by ~1 m per year (natural)
-Conservation: International park efforts since 1885
